source.title: Understanding Brain Mechanisms of Reactive Aggression

confidence_rationale: Anchors the CONSUMER and REGULATION side of the candidate stream. Reactive aggression is 'a response to social threat, provocation, or frustration, strongly associated with anger,' instantiated by the amygdala-hypothalamus-PAG acute-threat circuit and INHIBITED by prefrontal control (vmPFC/vlPFC/dlPFC); it is categorically distinct from proactive/instrumental aggression (planned, goal-directed, low-arousal). That maps onto the verdict's consumer set: the blocked-agency signal drives an assert/escalate response that must be gated by a regulatory channel (REE commitment-threshold / decommit, MECH-342), and the reactive-vs-proactive split warns REE not to conflate frustration-driven assertion with planned goal pursuit. Human clinical/review source, good quality; mapping is to the consumer architecture, hence 0.74.
failure_signatures: Reactive aggression (frustration/threat-triggered, high-arousal, anger) is doubly dissociated from proactive/instrumental aggression (planned, low-arousal, goal-directed); a REE model that routes a blocked-agency signal through the ordinary goal-pursuit/E3 trajectory machinery without a distinct high-arousal assert channel would mis-model the reactive response.

Reactive aggression is normally held in check by prefrontal inhibition (reduced vmPFC volume -> more physical aggression); a blocked-agency consumer with no regulatory/decommit gate would produce unchecked escalation -- the pathological (intermittent-explosive) phenotype, not adaptive assertion.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Reactive aggression is a response to social threat, provocation, or frustration, strongly associated with anger and high arousal, mediated by the amygdala-hypothalamus-periaqueductal-gray acute-threat circuit and regulated/inhibited by prefrontal cortex (vmPFC, vlPFC for emotional action control, dlPFC for holding control goals); it differs fundamentally from proactive/instrumental aggression, which is planned and goal-directed.
mapping.ree_translation: Grounds the consumer side of the candidate stream. The blocked-agency signal should drive an ASSERT/escalate response (the adaptive analogue of reactive aggression) that is explicitly GATED by a regulatory/decommit channel -- REE's commitment-threshold adjustment (ARC-016) and maintenance-time decommit (MECH-342). The reactive-vs-proactive dissociation tells REE the assert channel is distinct from ordinary z_goal-driven planned pursuit, supporting a separate affect row rather than a tweak to goal salience.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Human clinical/personality-disorder review of overt aggression; REE is a single-agent V3 substrate with no 'aggression' behaviour and no social target. The transfer is to the abstract CONSUMER architecture (high-arousal assert + prefrontal-gated inhibition/decommit), not to aggressive action. The SOCIAL-threat/provocation triggers in this paper are V4-scope; only the frustration trigger and the assert/regulate consumer split are V3-relevant.
mapping.source_context: Review of the neurobiology of reactive aggression in healthy and clinical (e.g. borderline, antisocial) populations; fMRI/structural and circuit evidence.

confidence_components.notes: Good source quality (Current Psychiatry Reports review). mapping_fidelity moderate: maps cleanly to the consumer/regulation architecture but the paper's behaviour (overt aggression) and several triggers (social provocation) are V4-scope, so only part of it bears on the V3 proxy. transfer_risk moderate-high: human social aggression -> single-agent REE assert/decommit.
